observation.visible_scene: A sunlit outdoor patio: a tall cylindrical gray planter topped with ornamental grass stands center-left on stone tiles, a wooden deck runs along the left, a gray table edge sits at the right, and a glass door/window behind the planter reveals an interior cat tree (rope-wrapped post with a fluffy white platform) and a pile of light pebbles at its base. A fluffy brown-and-white long-haired cat is positioned on the tiles to the right of the planter, facing the glass.
visible_changes: The framing tightens progressively: the left wall window and the right table edge slide out of view while the planter and cat grow larger, indicating a camera zoom-in / pan rather than scene motion.
For roughly the first 25 frames the cat stays seated upright, head tilted upward toward the cat tree, with its tail resting low behind it.
Between about frames 26 and 32 the cat rises from a sitting posture onto all four legs (front paws become visible and the body lifts).
As it stands, the tail transitions from a low curled position to a raised, extended position, and the body turns slightly more toward the camera/left; the cat keeps looking upward at the cat tree.
The planter, grass, deck, and interior cat tree/pebbles remain fixed in the scene; no contact between the cat and the glass occurs within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the cat is attending to above the cat tree, and whether it moves further after standing.
The identity and motion of the grayish shape at the base inside the glass (a second cat or a reflection).
Events before the cat sat down and after the excerpt ends.
uncertain_details: Whether the camera motion is a zoom, a dolly, or a pan (background shift supports motion but not its exact type).
Whether the interior gray form near the pebbles is a real cat or a reflection.
Any subtle swaying of the grass blades is not clearly resolvable frame-to-frame.
